summary: Orchestrator epoch skew causes staged-rollout cohort divergence and mixed variant routing
description: Customer (NimbleDocs) observed that during a staged canary rollout of redwood/gptx-13b-v2 some requests from the same tenant returned responses from both the old and new variants. Issue appears correlated with a control-plane orchestrator leader rotation that happened mid-rollout. Symptoms include mixed quality outputs for a small percentage of sessions, elevated 500 responses from the edge for ~7 minutes, and a billing spike due to duplicate request replay.
impact: Intermittent mixed-model responses for ~2% of requests for a subset of tenant sessions; increased 5xx errors for 7 minutes; customer-reported degraded user experience and unexpected usage billing spike. A single enterprise customer (dedicated) affected; potential risk to other rollouts if not fixed.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a staged rollout for model redwood/gptx-13b-v2 with 10% initial cohort.
2) Induce an orchestrator leader rotation by restarting the primary control-plane replica during the first 3 minutes of rollout.
3) Send a mixture of pinned and non-pinned requests for the same tenant session (streaming and non-streaming) and observe model variant in responses.
4) Observe routing snapshots and cohort assignments via /debug/route-snapshot for the tenant during rotation window.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: routing snapshot TTL and leader rotation created transient snapshot divergence across control-plane replicas leading to different route decisions at edge proxies.
Confirmed that two distinct route_snapshot versions (timestamps separated by ~52s) were concurrently considered authoritative by different edge nodes.
Observed orchestrator publish logic allows a new epoch to be published before all followers confirm last snapshot ack; followers that lagged kept serving older snapshot -> cohort split.
No evidence of KV-store corruption; manifests and snapshots present but epoch sequence gaps visible in orchestrator logs.
Customer traffic pattern (long-lived pinned sessions with streaming) amplified the symptom because session-affinity cached an edge-resolved variant for the duration of the stream.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer reported mixed outputs and billing spike, provided sample request IDs and timestamps. Asked SRE to triage.
Marcus Chen (SRE) 2026-03-12: Confirmed epoch mismatch in orchestrator logs; reproducer created in staging to validate leader rotation behavior.

Lena Rodriguez (Control-plane Eng) 2026-03-13: Found that follower ack path has a race where leader increments epoch and publishes snapshot before follower acks; pushing a hotfix PR to gate publish on ack quorum.

Marcus Chen (SRE) 2026-03-14: Deployed emergency configuration to increase route_snapshot_ttl and forced snapshot resync across all edge nodes for affected region; monitoring shows routing stabilized.
Customer (NimbleDocs) 2026-03-14: Confirmed user-facing errors reduced and quality inconsistencies resolved.
resolution: 1) Temporarily pinned NimbleDocs tenant to the legacy variant until stable snapshot resync completed.
2) Forced global snapshot resync command for us-east-1 edges and control-plane replicas at 2026-03-13T22:00Z.
3) Rolled back the canary for NimbleDocs and paused other staged rollouts until fix validated.
4) Merged hotfix (github.com/redwood/control-plane/pull/7890) that gates epoch publish on follower ack quorum; hotfix deployed to prod 2026-03-14.
5) Issued a billing credit estimate to NimbleDocs for duplicated requests; finance ticket created (linked INT-90421).
root_cause: Control-plane orchestrator could publish a new route snapshot epoch before a quorum of follower replicas acknowledged the previous epoch, producing epoch skew across replicas and resulting in inconsistent route resolution at edge proxies during leader rotation.
follow_up_tasks: 1) Add end-to-end guardrails: control-plane should expose a snapshot-consistency check that edges can query before committing route decisions.
2) Add automated canary hold if any epoch_gap > 1 detected during staged rollouts.
3) Improve metrics/alerts: track epoch divergence count and set a PagerDuty escalation at >0 for enterprise rollouts.
4) Postmortem and runbook update: document leader-rotation mitigation and resync steps; publish to confluence (add to related_confluence_pages).
5) Follow up with NimbleDocs CS for formal credit and communicate permanent fixes and timeline.
